summary:
Official Marvel sources describe the body makeup of several characters, and the chart can use some of it. Nothing gives a body-fat percentage or a tissue density in kg/m3. Key findings:

(1) Asgardian density is official. The Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe, Deluxe Edition (1985-86), as reprinted in the 2006 Essential volume 1, says: "Asgardian flesh and bone is about three times denser than similar human tissue, contributing to the gods' superhuman strength and weight." The 1987 trade paperback vol 4 and The Definitive Thor (Panini, 2011) have the same wording. DK's Marvel Encyclopedia (2014 and 2019) says "Their skin and bones are three times as dense as those of a human ... due to their density, weigh far more than humans of comparable size." Thor's 640 lb divided by 3 is about 97 kg (213 lb), which puts his score at an ordinary level (S about 20-22, against 60-67 as listed).

(2) Wolverine's adamantium is official: Marvel.com says it "adds an extra 105 pounds to his frame—or 47.6 kilograms" (300 lb with it, 195 lb without). I found no handbook figure, and "nearly 100 pounds" appears only in fan-wiki text.

(3) Colossus, armoured: the handbook calls the substance "of unknown composition but ... analogous to osmium and to carbon steel" and says he gains "additional mass from an unknown, perhaps extradimensional source". His body is not tissue, so he is not comparable.

(4) The Thing: the official wording is a rock-like or rocky skin, hide or exterior ("supple"). Nothing gives its mass.

(5) Hulk and Abomination: the handbook says gamma radiation "fortified his cellular structure and added, from some as yet unknown source, over 800 pounds of bone marrow and tissue" (Hulk) or "bone marrow and muscle tissue" (Abomination). So the added mass is officially tissue.

(6) Luke Cage: "very dense muscle and bone tissue, and steel-hard skin" (DK 2019) and "Superdense Body Mass" (Marvel.com), with no factor.

(7) Kingpin: "His great bulk does not consist of fat but of muscles ... as in a sumo wrestler" (handbook), and "Most of Fisk's bulk is actually muscle, not fat" (Marvel.com). The "9 pounds of fat" figure is fan-wiki only.

(8) For Superman, Batman, Darkseid, Doomsday and Bane, the DC sources (two DK books) say nothing about density or composition. Bane's Venom is described as a super-steroid. Density claims for Superman, Darkseid and Doomsday, and Black Panther's "denser tissue", come only from fan wikis.

(9) Body-fat percentage: none in any Marvel or DC source searched, as expected. The only statements are in words: Kingpin, and Angel's "body is virtually devoid of fat".

facts.notes: Exact OCR snippets from archive.org full-text search; these are lending-library scans, so only about 100 characters around each hit can be seen. Essential OHOTMU Deluxe vol 1 (2006): 'immortal like the Olympian gods), aging at an extraordinarily slow. rate upon reaching adult- hood. Asgardian flesh and bone is about three times denser than similar human...'. Same volume: 'times denser than similar human tissue, contributing to the gods' superhuman Strength and weight. An male'. Other entries in the same volume: '(Asgardian flesh and bone is about three times denser than similar human tissue, contributing to the Asgar- dians' superhuman strength and weight.) His Asgardian metabolism gives him super- human endurance', and 'injury (Asgardian flesh and bone is about 3 times denser than Earthly flesh and bone, accounting for Asgardians'...'. The 1987 vol 4 reads: 'and bone is about 3 times denser than similar human tissue, contributing to the Asgardians superhuman strength and weight.)'. The Definitive Thor Reloaded (2013): 'flesh, bone, and muscle possess about three times the density of the tissue of a human body.' The same 2006 volume's Asgard entry says 'common matter is considerably denser on an average. Con- sequently a chair made of Asgardian...' and 'water, flesh, bone, steel - all mat- . ter is denser and thus more durable'. Wording varies between 'three times denser' and '3 times as dense', so read it as a factor of about 3, not 4. Not confirmed: the issue number and page of each entry. The group entry sits in the part reprinting Deluxe #1-7, probably #1 (the A entries), unverified. No handbook gives a density in kg/m3. The fan wiki cites Thor & Hercules: Encyclopaedia Mythologica (2009) for 'skin, muscle, and bone tissues ... about three times as dense'; I did not fetch that book, so status reported. The fan-wiki infobox also gives an Asgardian 'AvgWeight 450 lbs', uncited (reported). Archive.org also holds unauthorised digital comic uploads that repeat this wording; I deliberately did not cite them.

facts.label: Thor: official weight converted to human-tissue-equivalent mass (official weight divided by 3)

sources.title: Marvel.com Thor (Thor Odinson) In Comics (640 lb, 6 ft 6 in)
Archive.org full-text search, Essential OHOTMU Deluxe vol 1: 'denser than similar human tissue'

facts.notes: Method: a body of the same size and shape made of ordinary tissue would weigh the listed mass divided by the density ratio: 290.3 / 3 = 96.8 kg (213 lb). S = 1.8 x FFM / H^3 and FFMI = FFM / H^2 at assumed fat of 0, 10 and 15% (body fat is unknown). Assumes all tissue is 3x as dense, following OHOTMU's 'flesh and bone'. If only skin and bone are denser (DK's wording), the correction is smaller. I have not computed that case, because it needs tissue mass fractions not researched here. A numerical observation only, which Marvel does not state: 213 lb is close to Donald Blake's 150 lb scaled isometrically to 6 ft 6 in (217 lb, existing key plausibility_metrics). Relies on existing builds.json keys thor (height and weight) and plausibility_metrics. Rounded to what the inputs support: 'about three times' carries perhaps one significant figure, so the 97 kg value is about plus or minus a third.

Also: 'Grimm's outward form mutates over his years as the Thing, changing from a lumpy hide to what appears to be individual rocks linked together'. The Marvel.com guide: 'From his original human form to his rocky exterior and beyond'. DK 2019: 'Ben's skin turned orange and rocky, and his strength grew'; powers 'Superhuman strength, endurance, and durability. He can lift 85 tons'. Official wording therefore names the skin, hide or exterior. Fan wiki (reported; these sentences cite no source): 'Body is covered with an orange, flexible, rock-like hide'; 'The mutagenic process caused his overall musculature, bone structure, internal organ composition, soft tissue structure, and skin to also greatly increase in toughness and density'; 'The rock-like composition of the Thing's body renders him highly resistant to physical injury.' I could not reach the OHOTMU Thing entry text: the Deluxe Thing entry is not in the searchable volumes, and full-text search for 'rocklike hide' found only Sanderson's Marvel Universe (1998), 'enormous strength and a nearly impenetrable, rocklike hide'. facts.notes:
These are my recommendations, built on the facts above; they are not official.
- Comparable means the listed mass is described as ordinary tissue, or nothing official says otherwise.
- Overstated means official text says part of the mass is not ordinary tissue, or the tissue is denser, so the score built from listed mass is too high. A factor is given only where a source gives a figure.
- Not comparable means the body is not tissue at all.
By character:
- Thor and Asgardians: divide by about 3.
- Wolverine: subtract the official 105 lb.
- Colossus, armoured: steel-like body.
- The Thing and Luke Cage: overstated by an unknown amount.
- Hulk and Abomination: the handbook calls the added mass bone marrow and (muscle) tissue.
- Juggernaut: no source says whether the 900 lb includes his helmet and armour.
- Darkseid and Doomsday: comparable only because nothing official says otherwise.
- Superman, Batman, Captain America and Black Panther: human-plausible, and no official density statement exists.

recommendations:
1. Thor and any Asgardian: mark overstated. Plot the main marker at the human-tissue-equivalent mass, 290.3/3 = 96.8 kg (213 lb). That gives S about 20-22 and plain FFMI about 22-25 at 0-10% fat.
